   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

         Mr. E.Chipchase
        47 Brunswick Road
     Broomvalley, Rotherham
     South Yorkshire S60 2RX

Dear Chris

I understand that cost keep
going up and I would have no
objection to paying more for the
+3 disc. If an economical price
as to be paid it would be worth
it. Where else can you get
information for the Spectrum at
the price you charge?

Having been retired for two
years and reached the age of
sixty seven, I find most
magazines today cater for games
and young people.

Having got that off my chest,can
I now tell you I use the +3 for
my part time commitment to my
social club. I am treasurer for
the Model Railway, Camera Club
and the Retired Members Section;
also secretary and treasurer of
the National P.S.V. Photographic
Competition.My wife is also the
agent for Vernons Pools and most
programs used for the agency are
my own BASIC.I also do a monthly
newssheet for the Social Club.
All this keeps me busy.My set up
is two +3s and a 120D printer.
Software include Tasman +3 W.P,
Masterfile,Tascalc, Wordmaster,
Headliner, Typeliner for D.T.P.
Anyone wishing an example of
what Typeliner can do; contact
me and I will send them some.

Now for my queries. Is it poss-
ible to couple the two computers
together by way of the S. port?
can the drive on one computer be
used as drive B? What is the
best drive for drive B to format
on 3 1/2 in. disc.

I am not a D.I.Y. man so every
bit of hardware would have to
fit without any difficulty. If
anyone has a second drive for
sale or monitor (Colour or B/W)
I would be pleased to hear from
them.

         Yours Sincerely

          E. Chipchase


Brian Cavers to E. Chipchase

There is no easy way to connect
your two Plus 3's so one can use
the other's drive as a 'B' drive
(although it may be possible in
CP/M) so your best bet is to get
a new 3.5" 1 megabyte drive.

You could try Mr. Craven, MICRO-
FORM, 191 Watling St. Road,
Fulwood, Preston, Lancs. PR2 4AE
who should be able to supply the
drive for around `79. Tell him
Brian Gaff of B.G. Services
recommended you try him and ask
for an 80 track, 3.5"  drive for
use as a Plus 3 'B' drive. It
might be wise to ring first on
0772 701248(you might also check
the odd "Watling St. Road" bit
of the address!).

An alternative supplier is EEC
of 18-21 Misbourne House, Chilt-
ern Hill, Chalfont St. Peter,
Bucks, SL9 9UE. However, Brian
Gaff tells me he thinks the
proprietor has dropped the "EEC"
title and is now trading under
his own name so you might ring
(EEC) first on 0753 888866.

The drive to ask for is the 3.5"
UNIVERSAL (MGT LIFETIME) drive
for a Plus 3. The last time I
saw this advertised it was `78
but you might check first. The
drives were probably a limited
stock from MGT so, again, it
would be wise to check they have
some left. An advantage of the
LIFETIME drive is that it can be
adapted for other computers such
as the Amiga, ST, QL etc.

The `70 to `80 price tag seems
to be the going rate for a cased
drive with a power supply (which
is what you need)but if you find
that too expensive the only
other source that I can suggest
is that you browse through the
PC magazine adverts at your
local newsagent. However, most
such adverts are for uncased
drives with no power supply.


If you obtain a drive then you
need BFORMAT from OUTLET 48 to
enable you to format the discs
to the full 700 - odd Kbytes. If
you use the normal +3 FORMAT it
will work but just give you the
standard 173K on the disc (even
if it is a one-meg disc).

You mentioned coupling the two
Plus 3's together via the serial
ports. I assume you mean so you
can link the drives but if you
mean to pass files from one +3
to the other then it is possible
but you need a null-modem cable
and software. One way is to use
two serial printer cables which
are coupled with a connector. If
you want to pursue this, contact
Brian Gaff of BG SERVICES (see
OUTBOARD) who can supply both
the cables and software.

                      - Brian

Just a few ideas to kick around

readers would not like member-
ship to decline to a serious
level and so if at all possible
try to spread the word one way
or another.

To all concerned...

PRINTER CONTROL CODES.

In WPs and such as OUTWRITE the
control codes in the form CHRS
27 X Y are held in a table of
codes and called as required by
some form of character or entry
in the text file.


There is usually some space left
to add extra codes but sometimes
space runs out. A method that
works with OUTLET and quite
possibly with other WPs to en-
able more codes to be held in
the table can be used where the
last character of the code is an
ASCI character (but will not
work if value is not a printable
character).

As an example the LC10 colour
printer uses the code ESC, "r",
n to set colour where n is a
value between 0 and 6 and can be
either a character code or the
ASCI character. IE ESC "r" CHRS
1 or ESC "r" "1". Now, if all 7
colours are to be set up in the
control code table they will use
up 7 spaces.

An alternative is to only put
the ESC "r" in the table then
when used in the text file put
in the code marker as normal and
immediately follow by the char-
acter for the colour required.
(Do not leave any space). The
LC10 does have a fully ASCI
character form for colour: (C)n
but the above method is only 2
characters against 6 in last
form to be typed in.

This principle can be extended
to other codes where the control
code is the same form for select
and de-select and the last char-
acter can be in ASCI.For examp-
le, select DRAFT or NQL. ESC "x"
"0" or ESC "x" "1" where the ESC
"x" will be in the table and the


"0" or "1" added in the text
file. This idea is only of real
benefit if space in the control
code table is tight and will not
work with such as select char-
acter size as the last value 0
to 6 is CHAR$ CODE not ASCI. The
LC10, however, again has the
form ((S))n to set size and if
wanted ((S)) could be put in the
table in the form 40,40,83,41,41
and n added in the text.

UNIDOS. A correspondent recently
mentioned problems with sector
errors while changing over to
Unidos on a +D. I have converted


a +D and two Disciples to Unidos
and regularly use a Disciple
with this DOS. I am not aware
that it causes sector problems
but in reconfiguring discs it
can show up discs that are al-
ready suspect. While the info
says the discs can be reconfig-
ured without loss of data, a
disc, or part of a disc can be
lost if the reconfigure fails
due to sector errors.

I've not bothered to reconfigure
any of my original discs such as
OUTLET as it is unlikely any of
the advanced functions will be
used with them. It is not nec-
essary to upgrade existing
discs to run under Unidos, it
only helps where certain types


of files are being SAVEd or a
lot of disc swapping is taking
place on SAVEs or COPYing files.
New discs are formatted under
Unidos in any case so are
automatically upgraded.There are
a few points where Unidos has
caused problems and they are
that early OUTLETS will not run
because they use KEYWORDS in
file names such as CODE. Unidos
rejects these as invalid.

Secondly, if a program uses POKE
@ 11 then this has been reversed
to GDOS. One other point is, I
have found that the AUTOLOAD
function on BOOT will not work
with my Disciple and MK1 128k
Spectrum. It is O.K. with the
Disciple and +2 also I recall +D
and the 128.

No problems with 48k Spectrums.
It seems to be something to do
with timings of the 128 ROM with
a Disciple fitted (or ULA or
something!) but this could well
have been sorted out now.

I have always found Nev Young
(S. D. Software) extremely
helpful after purchasing the
Unidos from him. All in all, the
advantages of Unidos have
outweighed the disadvantages.

         Malcolm Perry

From: Malcolm Goodman, LEEDS

Dear Brian and Ron,

I've got another idea for a pro-
gramming challenge that may be
of interest to readers of both
the Spectrum and SAM versions of
OUTLET.

If you were to add together
1234567890987654321 and
9876543210123456789 then the
answer would appear as
1.1111111+E19 which may be
adequate in some instances. But
what if you wish to see the
total as a discrete answer?

The challenge therefore is to
write a BASIC program that will


accept two numbers between 0 and
'megazillions',add them together
and print the answer in full,
without an 'E' in sight. If that
is too easy then there are al-
ways the other three options of
subtraction, multiplication and
division to get your teeth into.
Anyone out there fancy a go?

         Best Regards,

        Malcolm Goodman
P.S.
If you fancy a real challenge,
how about doing it in machine
code?

Now if I go back to BASIC and

Brian Cavers to Harry Hill

There appears to be a misunder-
standing regarding MINICHARS. It
is an on-screen font only - that
is, to make the text displayed
on screen clearer. It will not
affect the font printed by your
printer.To do that you must look
at your printer manual to see if
it has alternate fonts.Note down
what printer codes it needs to
switch to them. Now study your
Tasword +3 manual to see how to
insert these printer codes into
the text of your document. When
you then print the document the
codes will switch your printer
to the alternative font selected
at that point in the document.
Not all printers can change the
printed font.

There is a different version of
OUTDEX for each system and the
tape version will not work on a
+3 disc. You do not say if you
have tried. I am assuming you
have loaded OUTDEX and seen the
prompt to press L to load new
data? If you have tried, you may
have got "bad filename"?

I do not have a copy of the tape
version to hand but it should be
possible to convert by...
1. RESET
2. ENTER +3 BASIC.
3. ENTER MERGE "OUTDEX".
4. WAIT FOR "OK"
5. ENTER THIS NEW LINE...

120 IF K$="L" THEN CLS:
    MERGE "INDXDATA"

Then enter RUN and resave using
the UPDATE option. If no good,
buy +3 OUTLET EXTRA 1 with the
+3 version of OUTDEX.

I do not have any records here
of what tapes and what discs you
have so I am not sure what you
are trying to do. I thought it
sounded like you want to load
all the data from OUTLET +3
discs but you mention tapes as
well. Do you mean you want to
copy some early OUTLET tapes to
+3 disc? If so, it is very
difficult and time-consuming
else we would have done it
ourselves - so don't try! Please
write again and clarify if I've
misunderstood what you want to
do.
                      - Brian

From: F.G. Miles, WELWYN

Some brief notes on your replies
in OUTLET 64:

1) The SAVE @ sector error some-
times happens even when my pro-
gram's only using one disc drive
- but it was hardly ever a prob-
lem till I got a second drive.It
happens only occasionally and
only with two programs both of
which I wrote myself: the SORT
routine on my modified CATLOAD-
ER, when it's rewriting the dir-
ectory,and the IBU program which
I sent you some months ago, but
which I've now modified for two
drives - the modified version
occasionally makes the error,
mostly on track 0 sector 2 but
sometimes on other sectors also.

It never happens with QUIKCOP,
for example,though that switches
drives.

My programs use double SAVE @s -
QUIKCOP doesn't! I look forward
to hearing more about BETADOS.

2) Switching drives - you are
right, of course, about my care-
less errors. In programs I now
use LOAD @ d,0,1,0. This loads
track 0, section 1 into ROM,
which, of course, rejects it.

3) Centrifugal force. The stone
isn't pulling on the string,
whatever it feels like. If the
string was fastened to a hook
screwed into the wall, you pull
it and it pulls back: this is

Newton's Third Law, action and
reaction are equal and opposite.
But you don't say there's a
"mural force" acting on the
string. Same with the whirling
stone. I've never read Newton's
Principia, where he explains his
laws: maybe he makes it clear.


4) VAL$. I've given myself a
headache re-reading the old man-
ual and also the Neil Ardley/
Douglas Kindersley shortened
manual which came with the Spec-
trum 48+;both are thoroughly
unhelpful when it comes to
actually using the function,
but for once the shorter manual
is a bit clearer. (page 73)

I think you are right and the
suggestion made in ROM Index
about concatenating functions is
wrong, there's nothing you can
do with VAL$ that you can't do
with ordinary string concatena-
tions. VAL$ "a$" is just the
same as a$ VAL$ a$ is the same
as a$ with its quotes removed;
but it makes "Nonsense in BASIC"
unless a$ has doubled quotes, eg
a$ = """2+2""" VAL$ """2+2""" is
"2+2" VAL$ "2+2" makes
"Nonsense" again.

I can't see any point in this at
all and I'm going to have a
little rest now.
              - Francis G. Miles

Brian Cavers to Francis Miles

Reviews of BETADOS are coming
soon - perhaps next month but
the latest is that is does seem
to cure the disc corruption bug
and has lots of other goodies. I
have now ordered myself a copy!

Centrifugal force.I don't agree.
The stone IS pulling on the
string and the force can be
measured using a simple spring
balance. Any rational scientist
will tell you that if you use an
instrument that measures force
and it indeed indicates a force
is there and can even tell you
its size then, by golly, there
really IS such a force however
you try to explain it away.

If you weigh an object then you
would agree there is a force of
gravity. If someone discovers in
a future experiment that gravity
is not quite what we thought it
was (e.g., something wierd like
waves of times interacting with
conscious thought) then there
would STILL be a force we call
gravity no matter how it works
(at least, according to how we
define and use the word "force).

You refer to Newton's Third Law:
action and reaction are equal
and opposite. Clearly if you
pull on a string you are using
force and if your force is held
in balance, whether by a wall or
a rotating bucket, then there
MUST be an equal and opposite
force acting.

When people put forward views
that conflict with my own I
always try to have a little
humility and accept that it must
be possible for me to be wrong.
I therefore try not to just
react emotionally but to re-
examine my own convictions. I do
this over and over again. In the
case of centrifugal force I had
a degree of doubt to start with
but the more I think through the
views put forward the clearer it
seems to me that centrifugal
force MUST be a force! Sorry! If
a reader has a physics textbook
with the definition please write
in and put us out of our misery!

I'm going to have a little rest
now too!              - Brian

From: G. Caldwell, LONDONDERRY

Dear Brian or Ron,

I am desperate to learn BASIC
programming. Any books that I
come across in shops were for
the ZX81 or 16K Spectrums.

PRINTER CONTROL CODES.

In WPs and such as OUTWRITE the control codes in the form CHRS 27 X Y are held in a table of codes and called as required by some form of character or entry in the text file.

There is usually some space left to add extra codes but sometimes space runs out. A method that works with OUTLET and quite possibly with other WPs to en- able more codes to be held in the table can be used where the last character of the code is an ASCI character (but will not work if value is not a printable character).

As an example the LC10 colour printer uses the code ESC, "r", n to set colour where n is a value between 0 and 6 and can be either a character code or the ASCI character. IE ESC "r" CHRS 1 or ESC "r" "1". Now, if all 7 colours are to be set up in the control code table they will use up 7 spaces.

An alternative is to only put the ESC "r" in the table then when used in the text file put in the code marker as normal and immediately follow by the char- acter for the colour required. (Do not leave any space). The LC10 does have a fully ASCI character form for colour: (C)n but the above method is only 2 characters against 6 in last form to be typed in.

This principle can be extended to other codes where the control code is the same form for select and de-select and the last char- acter can be in ASCI.For examp- le, select DRAFT or NQL. ESC "x" "0" or ESC "x" "1" where the ESC "x" will be in the table and the

"0" or "1" added in the text file. This idea is only of real benefit if space in the control code table is tight and will not work with such as select char- acter size as the last value 0 to 6 is CHAR$ CODE not ASCI. Centrifugal force.I don't agree. The stone IS pulling on the string and the force can be measured using a simple spring balance. Any rational scientist will tell you that if you use an instrument that measures force and it indeed indicates a force is there and can even tell you its size then, by golly, there really IS such a force however you try to explain it away.

If you weigh an object then you would agree there is a force of gravity. If someone discovers in a future experiment that gravity is not quite what we thought it was (e.g., something wierd like waves of times interacting with conscious thought) then there would STILL be a force we call gravity no matter how it works (at least, according to how we define and use the word "force).

You refer to Newton's Third Law: action and reaction are equal and opposite. Clearly if you pull on a string you are using force and if your force is held in balance, whether by a wall or a rotating bucket, then there MUST be an equal and opposite force acting.

When people put forward views that conflict with my own I always try to have a little humility and accept that it must be possible for me to be wrong. I therefore try not to just react emotionally but to re- examine my own convictions. I do this over and over again. In the case of centrifugal force I had a degree of doubt to start with but the more I think through the views put forward the clearer it seems to me that centrifugal force MUST be a force! Sorry! If a reader has a physics textbook with the definition please write in and put us out of our misery!

Тексты для OUTLETTERS принимаются в любом виде: файлы текстовых процессоров (укажите, какого именно), машинописные или рукописные письма. ### PRINTER CONTROL CODES

В текстовых процессорах, таких как OUTWRITE, управляющие коды в формате `CHRS 27 X Y` хранятся в таблице кодов и вызываются по мере необходимости определенным символом или меткой в тексте файла.

Обычно там остается немного места для добавления дополнительных кодов, но иногда память заканчивается. Способ, который работает с OUTLET и, вполне возможно, с другими текстовыми процессорами, позволяя вместить в таблицу больше кодов, можно использовать тогда, когда последний символ кода является символом ASCII (но он не сработает, если значение не является печатным символом).

Например, цветной принтер LC10 использует код `ESC, "r", n` для выбора цвета, где `n` — это значение от 0 до 6, которое может быть либо кодом символа, либо ASCII-символом. Т.е. `ESC "r" CHRS 1` или `ESC "r" "1"`. Если задавать все 7 цветов в таблице управляющих кодов, они займут 7 позиций.

В качестве альтернативы можно занести в таблицу только `ESC "r"`, а затем при использовании в тексте вставить стандартный маркер кода и сразу за ним указать символ нужного цвета. (Пробел ставить нельзя). У LC10 есть полностью текстовая форма ASCII для цвета: `(C)n`, но описанный выше способ требует ввода всего 2 символов вместо 6 в последнем варианте.

Этот принцип можно применить и к другим кодам, где управляющий код имеет одинаковый формат для включения и выключения, а последний символ может быть в ASCII. Например, выбор DRAFT или NLQ: `ESC "x" "0"` или `ESC "x" "1"`, где `ESC "x"` будет находиться в таблице, а «0» или «1» добавляются непосредственно в текстовом файле. Эта идея полезна только в том случае, если место в таблице управляющих кодов сильно ограничено; она не сработает с такими вещами, как выбор размера символов, поскольку последнее значение от 0 до 6 — это `CHAR$ CODE`, а не ASCII. Впрочем, у LC10 снова есть формат `((S))n` для установки размера, и при желании `((S))` можно поместить в таблицу в виде `40,40,83,41,41`, а `n` дописывать в тексте.
